title: Signature study: HMAC compared with bcrypt
description: 1996 — HMAC: HMAC is a construction that turns any cryptographic hash function into a message authentication code using a secret key. compared with bcrypt (1999), This Signature comparative study sets the two side by side on design, security margin, and real-world use. bcrypt is an adaptive password-hashing function based on the Blowfish cipher's expensive key schedule. Filed as JAH-CRY-000015 in the JAH Cryptography Database archive.
